sections.html:
Cass County, Nebraska, runs along the Platte River on its north side and the Missouri River on its east, with Plattsmouth as the county seat and largest city. The 2020 census counted 26,598 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 27,657. Fifteen towns and villages sit inside the county, from Alvo and Avoca to Union and Weeping Water. Whether you live in Plattsmouth or in a small village, you deal with the same county Assessor and Treasurer, and both are in Plattsmouth.

The Assessor values more than 21,000 real estate parcels. Knowing which office does what saves a lot of phone calls once a sale is underway.

The Assessor values property and the Treasurer collects the tax. The Assessor's office is in the Annex at 145 N. 4th St., just north of the courthouse at the corner of N. 4th St. and Avenue A. It's open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 4:30 p.m., phone 402-296-9310.

The Treasurer's page shows the office at 446 Main Street, 2nd floor, with the same weekday hours and a property tax line at 402-296-9511. The office has moved recently, so confirm the location before you bring a payment.

  • A 24-hour drop box sits at 446 Main St on the northwest side of the building. Don't put cash in it.
  • The counter takes cash, check, money order and cards (extra fees apply).
  • Online payments go through Nebraska Taxes Online at nto.us.
  • Cards can't be used for tax sale redemptions.

On the valuation side, the Assessor handles about 1,300 personal property parcels, processes over 900 homestead applications and 150 permissive exemption applications, and answers about 10,000 information requests a year.

Delinquent Cass County tax turns late on May 1 and September 1. Check the statement for the county that sends it, since each Nebraska county sets its own calendar in practice.

The rate on delinquent tax comes from state law. When an owner redeems after a tax sale, the buyer of the certificate receives 14% simple interest from the sale date to the redemption date.

The Assessor is carrying out its required six-year review in 2026, and the new values apply to 2027. The Assessor's page says data collectors work from April through December 31, 2026 in these places:

  • Towns: Avoca, Manley, Nehawka, Union and Weeping Water villages
  • Rural townships: Mount Pleasant, Center, Weeping Water, Avoca/Nehawka and Nehawka/Liberty

Collectors wear orange reflective vests, carry county badges issued by the Sheriff's Office and drive county vehicles. They photograph and measure structures. If nobody's home, they leave a call-back slip on the door. Owners can return a property review questionnaire by mail or in the drop box on the west side of the courthouse.

If you own in one of those areas and plan to sell, use the visit to confirm that the square footage, finished basement and outbuildings on record match what's really there. Errors in that record affect the value your buyer will be taxed on.

Use Form 422. The Assessor's page links the form with instructions, the county has a separate Property Valuation Protest page, and the state's Tax Equalization and Review Commission handles later steps.

Religious, charitable and educational exemptions go to the Assessor for review.

The Assessor is an elected official on a four-year term who must hold a state certificate and complete 15 hours of continuing education each year.

sections.h2: How does the Cass County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels go to an auction of tax lien certificates held the first Monday in March at the Plattsmouth Community Center, 308 S. 18th St., starting at 8 a.m. The county advertises the delinquent taxes for three weeks in February in the Sarpy County Times.

  • Buyers pay a $25 registration fee and $20 per certificate.
  • A round robin format gives a randomly chosen first bidder the first parcel.
  • Buyers acquire a lien, not the property, and can't foreclose for three years.
  • The Treasurer doesn't issue treasurer's deeds, so foreclosure goes through the courts.
  • Parcels already sold, in bankruptcy or owned by a government body are left out.

Published amounts leave out delinquent interest and may cover several years. If your house is on the list, ask for a current payoff in writing. When the house sells, the title company clears that amount at closing.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short checklist
sections.html:
A seller with a Cass County house can head off most delays by sorting a few items first.

  • Call the Treasurer's property tax line at 402-296-9511 and ask for the current balance, including any tax that went delinquent on May 1 or September 1.
  • Ask whether the parcel appears on the advertised delinquent list. If it does, get a written payoff that includes interest, because the published figure leaves interest out.
  • If you live in a village or township on the reappraisal list, check the square footage, finished basement and outbuildings on file, and return the property review questionnaire if you received one.
  • File your homestead exemption application by June 30 if you qualify and haven't yet.
  • Have your deed information ready for the Register of Deeds, and plan on the documentary stamp tax at closing.

With those answers in hand, the title company can confirm payoffs quickly, and you can compare a listing against a cash offer using real net numbers. If a buyer needs the house by a certain date, share the list with them early. They'll see which items are settled and which still need a phone call to Plattsmouth, and nobody is guessing at the closing table. Ask the title company to send you the payoff letter in writing as well, and keep a copy with your closing papers.

sections.h2: Closing costs and the sale record
sections.html:
The Nebraska documentary stamp tax applies to the deed, at $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026. The grantor is liable, and the grantee or any agent presenting the deed may pay it. Deeds are recorded through the Cass County Register of Deeds, which has an online deed search.

The Assessor also keeps a sales file for every property sale in the county and compares it with its records. An unusually low price on a quick as-is sale can prompt a data collector's visit later.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Cass County house with unpaid tax, a reappraisal question or a lien and give a written offer. The title company confirms payoffs before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cass County property tax?
faqs.a: At the Treasurer's office, 446 Main Street, 2nd floor, Plattsmouth, in the drop box, or online through Nebraska Taxes Online. Cards carry extra fees and can't be used for tax sale redemptions.

faqs.q: When does Cass County property tax become delinquent?

faqs.a: Yes. The Assessor is doing its six-year review in 2026 for 2027 values, with data collectors working from April through December 31 in named villages and townships.

faqs.q: What form do I use to protest a Cass County valuation?
faqs.a: Form 422, which the Assessor's page links with instructions. The county also has a Property Valuation Protest page.

faqs.q: Does Cass County issue treasurer's deeds after a tax sale?
faqs.a: No. A certificate holder must foreclose through the courts, and statutory time limits apply to certificates.
